newsitem.title: USA: I2 wins $24 mln contract from TI.
newsitem.headline: I2 wins $24 mln contract from TI.

text.p: I2 Technologies Inc, a supply chain management firm, said Wednesday it won a $24 million contract to provide Texas Instruments Inc with software to keep track of its global semiconductor inventory.
I2, based in Irving, Texas, said Texas Instruments signed a multi-year licensing and development agreement for the use of its "Rhythm" supply management software.

Texas Instruments spokeswoman Kimberly Quirk told Reuters the chip giant would use I2's software "as a global planning system for our semiconductors", allowing it to meet customer demand while keeping inventories low.
She said Dallas-based Texas Instruments would begin installing the software in late 1998.
Market rumors of the deal had earlier pushed i2's shares up 7-3/8 to close at 42-5/8 on the Nasdaq National Market.
